L01.why: 'as to whether' is wordy; A could precede an independent clause opening with a whether-subject; none is ungrammatical in every frame

L02.why: 'you fertilize' shifts to second person, but could fit a conditional/imperative frame

L03.why: comma splice if 'three...' begins an independent clause, but could be an appositive list

L04.why: 'not...but because' parallelism favours 'but'; B could still fit a conjoined frame

L05.why: number/tense depend entirely on withheld subject

L06.why: 'it's own' is never correct: 'it's' = 'it is/has', and the possessive is 'its own'

L07.why: 'Namely' opening a sentence without a comma usually introduces a fragment, but not provably wrong

L08.why: 'having' cannot be a finite verb, but works in participial frames

L09.why: depends on withheld subject and tense

L10.why: 'that one anticipates' is awkward but can be a noun clause

L11.why: likely a parallelism item; all four can function as objects in some frame

L12.why: probably a dangling-modifier item where the committee must be the subject (D); but each option is a complete clause valid without an opening modifier

L13.why: 'is modeling' could clash with a parallel verb, but grammatical in some frame

L14.why: 'there' cannot be a possessive, but could fit as an adverb in some sentence

L15.why: semicolon before 'although' often yields a fragment, but valid if an independent clause follows the although-clause

L16.why: punctuation of restrictive vs nonrestrictive depends on sentence

L18.why: 'whoever ... that' looks redundant, but 'that' could be a demonstrative ('that committee'); D 'whom' can open a noun clause

L20.why: dash/comma must match an earlier mark and the verb its subject, both withheld

L21.why: pronoun/possessive choice depends on the antecedent and frame; 'it's' and 'they're' can be correct contractions

L22.why: likely needs a complement form, but all four fit some frame
